Instructions from: /home/pixel/code/htb-2026/web/AGENTS.md
# Web app

The web app is a Next.js 16 project (App Router, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS 4, ESLint), managed with pnpm. Run commands from `web/`:

- `pnpm dev`: dev server on http://localhost:3000
- `pnpm lint`, `pnpm typecheck` and `pnpm build`: the checks to run before each commit

Copy `.env.example` to `.env.local` and fill it in before running the app. It lists the AI Gateway key that Jev's audience scoring needs; without it, scoring falls back to keyword matching.

## Next.js version

Next.js 16 has breaking changes from earlier versions in APIs, conventions and file structure, so code written from memory of Next.js 15 or older may not work. Before writing routing, data-fetching, caching or config code, read the relevant guide in `node_modules/next/dist/docs/`, which matches the installed version. Breaking changes from 15 are listed in `node_modules/next/dist/docs/01-app/02-guides/upgrading/version-16.md`.

`agentRules: false` in `next.config.ts` stops `next dev` from writing its own block of agent instructions into this file.

## UI

UI components come from shadcn/ui (`base-nova` style, on Base UI). Add one with `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add <component>` from `web/`; it lands in `src/components/ui/`.

Load the `frontend-design` skill before UI work. It is vendored from Anthropic's `claude-plugins-official` marketplace, under the Apache 2.0 licence in its folder, `.agents/skills/frontend-design/` at the repository root.

## LLM calls

LLM calls and AI agents go through the Vercel AI SDK (`ai` plus a provider package), not a provider's own SDK.

## Checking frontend work

- Check a frontend change on the running dev server with Playwright or a browser before reporting it done: look at the page, use the changed flow, and read the console for errors.
- Before starting a dev server, check whether one is already running, by its process or by probing its port, and reuse it. A change to config, dependencies or env means stopping it and starting a fresh one. Never leave several instances running.

result.output: docs/status.md:11:- Built: onboarding form and results page, in `web/`, with live audience scoring and competitor research. Placement pricing remains mocked. The form is one fill-in-the-blank sentence ending in a city menu whose only city is New York, followed by New York's five boroughs as a fixed list. The results are a map of New York's census tracts with customers, competitors and a recommendations tab that opens by default, with a legend and clickable campaign markers at matched stations, addresses and approximate areas. Each marker shows its competitor's logo, loaded from the competitor's own website, and falls back to initials when the site's icon cannot be fetched. Solid markers identify current campaigns with a station or address match; dashed markers identify approximate, historical or undated campaigns. Markers open no popups: hovering a campaign marker highlights its row in the Competitors tab, clicking it switches to that tab and scrolls to the row, and clicking a row's location moves the map to the marker. Each mapped row shows the data-source attribution. The placements to buy are numbered markers that match their numbers in the list, shown on the gap and competitors layers but not the customers layer, because they are chosen from observed gaps when current campaign locations are available, or from audience fit otherwise. Hovering a placement on the map or in the list highlights it in both, clicking a row moves the map to it, and clicking a marker scrolls the list to its row. Tabs above the results column pick the layer for both the map and the column, in the order Customers, Competitors, Locations or Gap. The third tab is selected at the start and is named Locations until current campaigns have precise locations, then Gap. Switching tabs slides the highlighted tab across, and the map's colours change at once. The column shows only that layer's sections: Locations has the 5 best audience locations, while Gap has the 5 biggest observed gaps; both include up to 12 placements to buy, Customers has the 5 tracts with the most target customers and the weighted tract columns, strongest first, with those that count against the customer marked "less likely", and Competitors has the competitors, each with its logo on the right of the row, and their ads, with the agent's latest step while it searches and a note counting ads without a reliable location match and so absent from the map. Hovering a tract on the map names it and shows the current layer's value for it, and hovering a trait under Customers shows its exact weight in place of its measure. Verified on 8 November 2026 in commit `Add hover values to tract boxes and trait bars`: web lint, typecheck and build passed; the hover tooltips were not checked in a browser. Submitting the form moves the whole results view upward from below the screen over 1.2 seconds while the background gradient rotates steadily at 150 degrees per second, with the form visible behind it until the movement finishes. Reduced-motion preferences skip the visible movement. Verified on 8 November 2026 in commit `Speed up gradient rotation during results transition`: desktop and 390-by-844 mobile browser checks showed the gradient turning 60 degrees after 400 milliseconds, a 1.2-second slide, no horizontal overflow, and both animations removed when the results settled. Edit restores the original gradient. Reduced motion disabled rotation, and the browser had no console errors. Web lint, typecheck and build passed. The results fill the window: the map fills the left two thirds and stays in view while the column scrolls in the right third, and on phones the map sits on top at 55% of the screen height. Verified on 7 November 2026 in commit `Animate results upward after form submission`: desktop and 390-by-844 mobile browser checks confirmed that the results and their content move together, settle at the top without horizontal overflow, and preserve the form answers on Edit. Reduced motion completed immediately, invalid amounts blocked submission, and the browser had no console errors. Web lint, typecheck and build passed. The column opens with a one-line summary of the brief and an Edit button that brings the form back with its answers kept. Submitting a completely empty form runs the sample fintech budgeting-app brief with a $3,000 monthly budget in New York. Entering any field or changing a dropdown keeps full required-field and numeric-pattern validation. There is no separate `/map` route. Verified on 7 November 2026 in commit `Use sample defaults for empty form submissions`: a blank submission showed the sample map and 12 placements; each individually filled field and a changed payment dropdown blocked incomplete submission; numeric patterns still blocked invalid amounts; a complete custom brief submitted its own values and Edit kept them; `/map` returned 404. The browser had no console errors, and all 26 tests, lint, typecheck and build passed. Faked: placement costs, measurement methods and minimum spends are invented. Real: the audience fit scores are weighted sums of the real scaled tract columns, and the placements are real kiosks and shelters selected across eligible tracts in descending observed gap-score order when current campaigns have precise locations, or descending audience fit otherwise, with one per tract and at least 500 metres between them. The column weights come from Jev through AI Gateway when `AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY` is set in `web/.env.local`, or on a Vercel deployment through its OIDC token: one request asks a five-level score question per column, from strongly against to strongly for, and each weight runs from -1 to 1, the probability-weighted level. Without either, or when Jev fails or takes over 20 seconds, the weights come from keyword matching on the target customer, and the Customers tab says so. Verified on 8 November 2026 with the sample brief: the Customers tab said "weighted by Jev", and the scoring request, Jev plus the tract arithmetic, took 892 ms. For "young professionals in tech who rent with roommates", the strongest weights were jobs in information (+0.94), residents aged 20 to 34 (+0.89) and median age (-0.83). Jev isn't on AI Gateway's free tier, so the key's Vercel team needs purchased AI Gateway Credits, and a card Vercel can verify. The browser computes competition per tract from its distance to each confirmed current campaign's matched station or street address, falling to about a third at 1 km, and the gap as audience fit times one minus competition; that formula is a first version, not a decision. The UI imports audience scoring, streamed competitor research and placement lookup through `web/src/lib/api.ts`, with types in `web/src/lib/contract.ts`. Placements appear after audience scoring and are re-ranked when research finishes. On 7 November 2026, the live energy-drink flow returned three competitors and three source-linked campaign findings. Their dates or station locations were unknown, so none lowered the gap scores. The production sample fallback showed three recorded competitors and its capture-date label; a different brief received no recorded findings. Both browser flows had no console errors. Verified in `2a85115`. Verified on 8 November 2026 in commit `Show competitor logos in the list and on campaign markers`: web lint, typecheck, build and all 32 tests passed, and the logo endpoint returned a PNG for each of the sample run's three competitors.
